A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same three-camera relative-pose work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplements support reliable comparison despite substantial changes in title, scope, and organization.

before.justification: V3 reports original real-scene evaluations, synthetic noise and outlier experiments, learned-correspondence results, and runtime measurements in Section 4 and the supplement.

after.justification: V4 reports original synthetic geometry experiments, ablations, and real-scene PoseLib and GC-RANSAC evaluations in Section 4 and supplementary Sections 6–8.

M1.justification: V4 adds the affine-camera 4p3v(A) solver and early non-minimal refitting (ENM), which refits two-view geometry before triangulation and third-camera registration. It removes v3's learned-correspondence solvers and shared-unknown-focal-length solvers. The original mean-point construction, shifted variants, filtering, and four-point refinement remain.

E1.justification: V4 adds evaluation on Aachen Day-Night v1.1 and controlled scenarios varying camera angles, camera distances, scene depths, and noise distributions. It removes evaluation of the shared-unknown-focal-length task. PhotoTourism, Cambridge Landmarks, ETH3D noise experiments, and two-view pose estimation already occur in v3 and are retained.

E2.justification: Alongside retained HC and 5pt+P3P baselines, v4 Table 2 evaluates 5pt+P3P with ENM, with refinement/filtering, and with both. The 6pt+P3P baseline and joint 5PC noise comparator disappear with their corresponding comparisons. Virtual-correspondence oracle controls are removed; the Nistér–Schaffalitzky oracle remains qualitatively evaluated in Section 8.6.

E3.justification: The selected shift changes from 0.04 to 0.08 times the longest triangle dimension. The ETH3D noise sweep expands from 0–4 to 0–16 pixels. Two-view RANSAC evaluation changes from GC-RANSAC in v3 Table 4 to a PoseLib iteration sweep in v4 Figure 10, and v4 introduces explicit 3/5/10-pixel threshold sweeps. These constitute substantial protocol revisions.

E4.justification: V4 adds controlled geometric sensitivity studies, Gaussian-versus-uniform noise tests, ENM ablations, and RANSAC-threshold sensitivity analyses. It revises the outlier study to Notre Dame at 40%, 60%, and 80% inliers, replacing earlier scenes and settings including 20% inliers. Most mean-point heatmaps remain, but v3's synthetic/Shop Facade heatmaps and quantitative oracle analyses are removed.

E5.justification: V3 Table 1 reports mean errors with accompanying ± values; v4's corresponding table drops these variability entries and reports medians and 20th percentiles. Boxplot quantiles and Gaussian fitting remain. Neither version reports repeated-seed uncertainty estimates or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Main and supplementary results are extensively replaced or expanded. For example, PhotoTourism Table 2 reports AUC@10 of 70.47 for 4p3v(M±δ)+R+F in v3 and 76.87 in v4, with revised settings including δ; this is not an established same-setting gain. V4 adds affine, ENM, and Aachen results, while learned, shared-focal, and quantitative oracle result entries disappear.

T1.justification: The epipolar-bound lemma and its proof are retained. V4 Section 6.2 adds a targeted algebraic derivation showing why the mean-point constraint is redundant for affine geometry but supplies an independent constraint for perspective geometry. V3's general minimal-configuration counting equation is removed. These are limited theoretical changes rather than a replacement of the central proof.

C1.justification: V3 claims contributions covering calibrated and partially calibrated cameras, virtual correspondences, and preliminary learned prediction. V4 redefines the contribution around two calibrated-camera solver families and their practical integration into RANSAC. Its abstract explicitly conditions state-of-the-art performance on local optimization and introduces the claim that mean-point solvers are more robust and accurate than affine solvers.

C2.justification: V3 discusses small-overlap instability and proposes uncertainty propagation or better learned correspondences. V4 replaces that discussion with explanations of error propagation, ENM, and differing local-optimization behavior in PoseLib and GC-RANSAC, and claims scene dependence becomes negligible after ENM. It also discusses ENM's applicability limits and explicitly qualifies the two-view solvers as not outperforming the five-point solver.

D1.justification: V4 changes code access from a future availability promise to a repository link stated to be available. It specifies ENM's SVD/QR construction, GC-RANSAC's PROSAC sampling and DLSPnP refitting, stopping/threshold details, and HC loading overhead. V3's extensive network architecture, normalization, optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size, and training-data documentation is removed with the learned branch.

R1.justification: V4 substantially expands positioning around affine and para-perspective approximations, including new references to Horaud, Oberkampf, and weak-perspective projection, and a fuller discussion of the already-cited Pritts approach. It revises comparisons with epipole-search methods and removes neural-method references such as NeFSAC, PointNet, and Set Transformer. This exceeds bibliographic updating.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, and method narrative are extensively rewritten. The method section shifts from calibrated/partially calibrated branches to approximate solvers and practical refinements. The supplement is reorganized around geometry, ablations, and real-data experiments, replacing its earlier mean-point/network/experiment organization. Author and affiliation text also changes.

P2.justification: V4 restructures Table 1 around four solvers with and without ENM and converts Table 2 into a full-width, three-dataset comparison. It adds geometric-sensitivity and threshold/ENM plots and removes the network diagram and partially calibrated displays. V3 Figures 2 and 6 are consolidated into v4 Figure 11, while selected retained heatmaps appear in the main text.

improvement.justification: V3 documents scene-dependent behavior but largely leaves individual geometric factors untested. V4 directly studies those factors and threshold sensitivity, explains and ablates ENM, and evaluates strengthened 5pt+P3P baselines, substantially improving validation of the calibrated-camera contribution. The constraint derivation and stated code availability further improve understanding and reproducibility. Removing partially calibrated and learned extensions and quantitative oracle controls reduces breadth and diagnostic evidence, but the stronger validation and practical guidance provide a substantial net improvement.
